title: Development of tensile strength methodology for murine skin wound healing
author: Bellare, Epperly, et al.

steps.title: Build 2‑blade punch
steps.instruction: Assemble a 2‑blade punch using a 15 mm wide aluminum spacer between the two blades and 3 mm thick spacers on the outer surfaces to keep the blades upright; secure the assembly with a rubber band on a clear polycarbonate slab, spread epoxy on all contacting surfaces with a wooden applicator, and cure the epoxy in an oven at 60 °C overnight.

substeps.instruction: Place a 15 mm wide aluminum spacer between the two blades.
Add 3 mm thick spacers on the outer surfaces of the blades.
Hold the construct together with a rubber band on a clear polycarbonate slab.
Apply epoxy to all contacting surfaces using a wooden applicator.
Cure the epoxy in an oven set to 60 °C for overnight (≈12 h).

steps.title: Build 11‑blade punch
steps.instruction: Construct an 11‑blade punch by inserting 1.75 mm thick spacers between each of the eleven 0.25 mm thick blades to yield 2 mm wide skin sections, add 3 mm outer spacers on the first and eleventh blades, secure with a rubber band on a polycarbonate slab, apply epoxy, and cure overnight at 60 °C; the punch is ready for use within 24 h.

substeps.instruction: Place 1.75 mm thick spacers between each of the 11 blades (blades themselves 0.25 mm thick).
Add 3 mm thick outer spacers to the first and eleventh blades.
Secure the entire assembly with a rubber band on a polycarbonate slab.
Spread epoxy on all contacting surfaces.
Cure the epoxy in an oven at 60 °C overnight (≈12 h); use within 24 h.

steps.title: Prepare skin strips
steps.instruction: Place square skin specimens in a PBS‑filled Petri dish, transfer each onto a 3 mm thick rubber sheet on a large polyethylene block, cut a 15 mm wide rectangle centered on the wound with the 2‑blade punch (using a ruler for alignment), then orthogonal to the incision use the 11‑blade punch to produce ten 2 mm × 15 mm strips, rinse punches with alcohol between specimens, and keep strips in PBS while preserving cephalad‑caudal orientation.

substeps.instruction: Put the skin specimen in a Petri dish containing phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS).
Transfer the specimen onto a 3 mm thick rubber sheet placed on a large polyethylene block.
Position the 2‑blade punch (15 mm blade spacing) over the skin; align with a ruler so the wound is centered between the two cut edges.
Manually press the 2‑blade punch down until the blades penetrate the rubber sheet, fully sectioning the rectangle.
Align the 11‑blade punch (2 mm spacing) orthogonal to the incision and cover the entire rectangle.
Press the 11‑blade punch manually to generate ten strips, each 2 mm wide and 15 mm long.
Rinse both punches with alcohol between each specimen.
Transfer the strips to a PBS‑filled Petri dish, maintaining their cephalad‑caudal orientation.

steps.title: Tensile test strips
steps.instruction: Subject each PBS‑immersed skin strip to tensile testing until failure, recording the failure load or stress as the measure of tensile strength.
